readout_other: Visual evoked potentials (surface electrode over primary visual cortex); brain temperature by thermocouples
direction_notes: Ultrasound alone did not significantly modify the averaged VEP; applied during acute hypoxia it kept the VEP response near normal (protective), and whole-body heating did not reproduce this.
safety_notes: Brain temperature was measured at the surface, 11 mm and 18 mm depth during 5 min of sonication; the 18 mm site reached 40.4 C under normoxia and 41.6 C under hypoxia.

exposures.label: 1 W/cm2 SATA, 1036 kHz, applied to exposed cat brain

target.label: brain exposed by removing a 3.9 cm diameter portion of the calvareum

timing.protocol_description: For Phase 3 the ultrasound generator was turned on one minute prior to the commencement of the two-minute hypoxic phase and turned off after the hypoxic episode; continuous versus pulsed mode and exposure duration are not stated for the VEP experiments (temperature measurements used five minutes of exposure).

source_quotes.n_subjects: The experiments were performed in nine cats in three phases:
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: A piezoelectric ceramic element 2.5 cm in diameter was excited to generate ultrasound at a resonant frequency of 1036 kHz.
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.ispta_w_cm2: The intensity of the applied ultrasound was 1 W/ cm² SATA (Spatial Average Temporal Average) at a frequency of 1036 kHz.

flags.reason: Reported as spatial-average temporal-average (SATA) intensity, measured in a water tank at the position of the proximal brain surface; recorded in the ispta field.
Ultrasound applied through water over the exposed dura of both hemispheres (unfocused applicator, 2.5 cm element); recording electrode over primary visual cortex. Target term is a judgement.
Continuous or pulsed mode not stated for this study.
Transducer maker not named; described as a piezoelectric ceramic element in an acrylic applicator, system described in an earlier paper.
